requirements.requirement: Create/configure opsadmin on node1 with the specified SSH public key installed for access
requirements.summary: opsadmin user created (uid 1000, /bin/bash shell), ~/.ssh directory created with 0700 permissions owned by opsadmin, and authorized_keys installed with exactly the specified ed25519 key (600 permissions, opsadmin ownership). Verified again post-restart, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password and keyboard-interactive auth) on node1
requirements.summary: A drop-in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf sets PubkeyAuthentication yes and disables PasswordAuthentication/KbdInteractiveAuthentication/ChallengeResponseAuthentication; sshd -t validated syntax and sshd was reloaded. Effective config (sshd -T) confirms pubkeyauthentication=yes, passwordauthentication=[REDACTED], kbdinteractiveauthentication=no both before and after a full node restart. A live SSH attempt without a matching key was rejected with only 'publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic' offered (no password prompt), repeated identically post-restart.

overall_summary: Both material requirements — creating opsadmin with the exact specified public key and enforcing key-only SSH authentication — are directly and repeatedly verified through configuration inspection and live SSH auth-method tests, both before and after a full node restart that demonstrates persistence. The mandatory restart evidence protocol is complete and coherent: pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, observed unreachability, a changed boot identity matching the global before/after cross-check, and full post-restart recovery of sshd, the opsadmin account, and the key-only policy. Hygiene is good aside from one small leftover log file from the reboot command.
limitations: A password-based SSH attempt was not directly tested (only a key-based attempt without a matching key was tried); reliance is on sshd -T output confirming passwordauthentication=[REDACTED] rather than an observed password-prompt rejection.
opsadmin's shadow password lock ('!') is supplementary hardening beyond the literal task wording but does not detract from the requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (useradd, .ssh/authorized_keys creation, sshd_config.d drop-in, sshd reload, opsadmin password lock via shadow, and the single bounded shutdown -r now) map directly to the task requirement or to the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol, and no failed/conflicting services or damaged package state resulted (failed-services and package-health observations are clean both before and after). The restart was bounded and fully recovered (boot_id 0581c914...->737850eb..., sshd active, config and keys intact). One minor unnecessary residue: /tmp/reboot.log was created by the backgrounded shutdown command's output redirection and was left behind rather than cleaned up post-verification (cmd-39b5a0fb29be482b); this is low-risk, non-sensitive leftover state, not reverted.
